# Data Dictionary — Raw Transactions Dataset
**File:** `data/raw/transactions.csv`  
**Generated by:** `ml/data/dataset_generator.py`  
**Format:** CSV, one row per transaction  
**Purpose:** Synthetic dataset simulating ISO 8583 payment authorisation messages for fraud model training

---

## Column Reference

### Identifiers
> These columns are dropped during preprocessing. They carry no predictive signal once card-level behavioural features are computed.

| Column | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `transaction_id` | string | `t_a3f9c12b8d01` | Unique transaction identifier. Prefix `t_`. |
| `card_id` | string | `c_7e2a91fc3b44` | Unique card identifier. Prefix `c_`. Used to group card history during feature engineering. |
| `merchant_id` | string | `m_0d4b77a21e98` | Unique merchant identifier. Prefix `m_`. Target-encoded as fraud rate during preprocessing. |
| `terminal_id` | string | `term_5c1a88f2b309` | Physical terminal identifier. Dropped — no model signal beyond what pan_entry_mode captures. |

---

### Transaction Core (ISO 8583 fields)

| Column | Type | Example | ISO 8583 DE | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `timestamp` | datetime | `2025-01-14T03:22:11` | DE 12 / DE 13 | Transaction date and time. UTC. Used to derive time features and enforce chronological split. |
| `transaction_amount` | float | `143.50` | DE 4 | Amount in the transaction currency. Not cross-currency comparable — use `enriched_amount_usd` for comparisons. |
| `transaction_currency` | string | `KES` | DE 49 | ISO 4217 currency code of the transaction. |
| `enriched_amount_usd` | float | `1.11` | — (derived) | `transaction_amount` converted to USD using fixed synthetic exchange rates. Use this for all amount comparisons and model features. Not a standard ISO 8583 field. |
| `transaction_type` | string | `purchase` \| `withdrawal` | DE 3 | Type of transaction. |
| `channel` | string | `ECOMMERCE` \| `POS` \| `ATM` | DE 18 | Channel through which the transaction was initiated. |
| `pan_entry_mode` | string | `CHIP` \| `CONTACTLESS` \| `MAGSTRIPE` \| `ONLINE` | DE 22 | How the card number was captured. CHIP = EMV cryptogram verified (safest). MAGSTRIPE = no cryptogram, fully clonable (riskiest). ONLINE = CNP, no physical card. |
| `authentication` | string | `BIOMETRICS` \| `OTP` \| `PIN` \| `CVV2` \| `NONE` | DE 22 / DE 55 | Authentication method used. Ordered by strength: BIOMETRICS > OTP > PIN > CVV2 > NONE. |
| `card_present` | int | `0` \| `1` | DE 61 | Fixed terminal attribute (not per-transaction). 1 = card-reading terminal (POS/ATM), 0 = CNP. Dropped during preprocessing — signal captured by `pan_entry_mode` and `channel`. |
| `cardholder_present` | int | `0` \| `1` | DE 61 | Fixed terminal attribute (not per-transaction). Reflects terminal type (attended vs unattended), not whether the legitimate cardholder was physically present. Dropped during preprocessing. |

---

### Card & Issuer

| Column | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card_type` | string | `Debit` \| `Credit` \| `Prepaid` | Card product type. Prepaid cards have higher CNP fraud propensity (weak identity binding). |
| `issuing_bank_country` | string | `USA` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country of the card-issuing bank. Used only to derive `cross_border`. Dropped after feature engineering. |

---

### Merchant

| Column | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `merchant_category_code` | string | `7995` | MCC code identifying the merchant's business type. **Not a number** — treat as a categorical identifier. Target-encoded as historical fraud rate during preprocessing. High-risk MCCs: 7995 (gambling), 4829 (money transfer), 6012 (financial institution), 5933 (pawn), 5542 (fuel/unmanned). |
| `transaction_country` | string | `GBR` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country where the transaction occurred. Used to derive `cross_border`. Dropped from target encoding (fraud rate differences across synthetic countries are sampling noise, not real risk signal). |
| `transaction_city` | string | `London` | City of the transaction. Too granular for model signal — dropped during preprocessing. |

---

### Verification Results

| Column | Type | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cvv2_result` | string | `MATCH` \| `NOT_PROVIDED` \| `NOT_APPLICABLE` | CVV2 verification result. Only meaningful for ECOMMERCE (CNP). POS/ATM = `NOT_APPLICABLE` (chip handles card verification). `NOT_PROVIDED` = card-on-file or MIT transaction where CVV2 was not submitted. Hard declines (NO_MATCH) never reach fraud scoring — not present in this dataset. |
| `avs_result` | string | `FULL_MATCH` \| `PARTIAL_MATCH` \| `NOT_PERFORMED` | Address Verification System result. Only available in USA and GBR for ECOMMERCE. All other countries = `NOT_PERFORMED` (no AVS infrastructure). Hard declines not present. |

---

### Label

| Column | Type | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `is_fraud` | int | `0` \| `1` | Ground truth fraud label. 1 = fraud. Overall rate: ~3–5% of transactions. Pre-assigned via a global fraud budget before generation to ensure stable distribution. |

---

## Key Design Decisions

**Fraud budget:** `TARGET_FRAUD = int(N_TRANSACTIONS × uniform(0.03, 0.05))` slots are pre-assigned before generation. Fraud does not emerge from random chance — it is deterministically placed, ensuring stable fraud rate across runs.

**Risk engine (hidden):** A hidden internal risk score (MCC risk + channel risk + entry mode risk + geography + velocity) influenced which transactions were assigned as fraud. This score is never written to the dataset — it shapes the data distribution without being a feature.

**Watchlist pre-emption:** Watchlisted cards and merchants are declined upstream before fraud scoring in real systems. They are therefore absent from this dataset — rows here represent only transactions that passed the watchlist check.

**No country risk tiers:** Geographic risk is captured only by `cross_border` (mismatch between issuing country and transaction country). No per-country risk scores are assigned — that would encode geographic bias into training data.

**`cardholder_present` is a terminal attribute:** It reflects whether the terminal type is attended or unattended (DE 22/DE 61), not whether the legitimate cardholder was physically present. It is dropped during preprocessing.
